away.name: Dylan Garand
away.news: Joonas Korpisalo made his season debut in New York's previous game, returning from a lower-body injury. Still, the team will likely continue to rely on Garand, at least semi-frequently. The 24-year-old Garand was solid in his most recent outing, saving 23 of 25 shots (.920 SV%) in a 3-2 win over the Philadelphia Flyers. The rookie goalie has had his share of ups and downs this season, but he has saved 55 of 58 shots (.948 SV%) during a two-game winning streak. The Rangers enter Monday's action as +141 road underdogs against an Edmonton Oilers team that defeated them 4-1 earlier this month.

home.name: Devon Levi
home.news: Levi returned from a two-week absence due to a lower-body injury on Saturday and played well, saving 20 of 22 shots (.909 SV%) in a 4-2 win over the Vancouver Canucks. Tristan Jarry played well during Levi's absence, arguably his best stretch of play as an Oiler, but Head Coach Mike Babcock reaffirmed his trust in Levi, returning him on Monday against the New York Rangers. The 24-year-old Levi has a 2.97 GAA and .889 SV% in eight games (7-1-0). The Oilers enter Monday's outing as -157 home favourites against a Rangers team on a three-game winning streak.

away.name: Joseph Woll
away.news: Woll had a chance to earn more playing time after a poor start to Dan Vladar's season, but he has struggled in recent outings, while Vladar has turned things around. The 28-year-old Woll was serviceable in his most recent outing, saving 26 of 29 shots (.897 SV%), but he still lost 3-2 to the New York Rangers. Woll has a 3.12 GAA and .899 SV% in nine games this season (1-6-2). The Flyers enter Monday's contest as -133 road favourites against a last-place Vancouver Canucks team that has scored two or fewer goals four times during a five-game losing streak (0-5-0).

home.name: Leevi Merilainen
home.news: Merilainen has allowed three or more goals in 10 consecutive games (1-8-1), yet, sadly for the Canucks, he remains more reliable between the pipes than Kevin Lankinen. The 24-year-old Merilainen was serviceable in his most recent outing, saving 26 of 29 shots (.897 SV%), but still lost 4-2 to the Edmonton Oilers. He has a 3.87 GAA and .862 SV% in his last four games (0-4-0). The Canucks enter Monday's contest as +120 home underdogs against a Philadelphia Flyers team that extended its losing streak to three games last night (0-2-1) with a 4-3 overtime loss to the Calgary Flames.

home.name: Yaroslav Askarov
home.news: Askarov played some of his best hockey at the NHL level through the end of October, but even his success didn't help the struggling Sharks. Now, 24-year-old Askarov is battling his own adversity, allowing 11 goals on 54 shots (.796 SV%) in his last two games (0-2-0). He has a 3.35 GAA and .885 SV% in 12 games this season (4-8-0). The Sharks enter Monday's game as +126 home underdogs against a New York Islanders team on a three-game losing streak (0-2-1).
